title: Armstrong asking Alcorn to join his band
summary: Louis tried to recruit Alcorn for his band in the 1940s, and Alcorn declined; he had dreamed of playing with such men.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Some of those stubborn guys we stayed with. I mean, that was 50 years ago. It's a long time. Did you ever... Put it down. Did you ever play with Louie in this group? No, I had a chance to go with Louie. When Louie came from here, Louie tried to get me to come in the band then. I used to be a first trumpet player too.
When was this now? Um... Still in the thirties? Forties? Forties? Yeah.

It had Louie Russell's band back then. Um... Um... Because Louie used to be a band all the time. He would... Well, he would sing all things. He would sing all things. He would sing all things by himself. He would tell you what he would be. And Louie Russell's band kept going on. So they came from here and Louie told me, Sabbath one, he said, Oh, the phone had a... I said, man, Sabbath one. They had two bands tonight. Their band was playing out again. They were sitting in the desk. And he said, They were talking to me. They were talking to me. They were talking to me. They were talking to me. They were talking to me. So... I looked into the band. And he said, We got a Troublem player. We got a Troublem player. For Troublem player. For their skates. For their Troublem player. So he had a Louie Russell Wilson line. That was two Troublem players. I said yeah, the Louis Russell wants to mind the upskins, he said, two trips. I said, why don't you come here and do it? I said, well, I've been out there, man. I've got seven, eight years. I've been going on that road. They've got to keep doing them going all the time in one night. They go on a regular job and stay a week, that's a long time. It cost so much money to hold a band like that. So, trying to do spots could have folded half, Louis was going to be a big band in there. So, I told him, I said, well, that was one of the first times, one of the greatest things I've ever had. Louis asked me to come down from the band.
That is quite a compliment. It was, you see.

And I thought it was great, but I said, well, this one time Louis asked me, I had to discipline. Because I never, I always thought from when I first started, I was praying. And someday I'd play with all those guys. I used to say it all the time. So, someday I'll play with those guys. And during the 15th tournament, I played with everyone. You see. And I was saying that as a youngster, maybe I was talking from the top of my head, but I was, I know they were so great over me and so far up over me, I didn't, I thought someday I'd be good enough to play with them. You see. But that's your dream. So, I didn't wake up, I just kept on dreaming or anything. But he did ask me to do that.
